summary: Evaluate shared neural representations and brain-model comparisons without confusing useful prediction with biological explanation.
outcomes: Compare a pretrained neural model against matched simpler baselines.
Distinguish transfer, representation similarity and mechanistic explanation.
sequence: Define what should transfer across sessions or datasets
Represent spikes, fields and metadata for model input
Introduce masking, contrastive and generative objectives
Audit pretraining data overlap and modality mismatch
Compare likelihood, decoding and biological tests
Identify unresolved scale and interpretability questions

visual.question: Is this transfer performance genuinely on unseen neural data?
visual.interaction: Reveal pretraining overlap and evaluate synthetic dataset-shift scenarios.

practice.task: Write an evaluation protocol for a neural foundation-model claim.
practice.success: Includes data-overlap checks, compute-matched baselines, held-out domains and a falsifiable biological claim.
